key_insight: Task-specific quality gating for OCT choroid segmentation works better with learned image representations than with traditional scalar image-quality metrics.
clinical_relevance: More reliable scan filtering could improve the consistency of retinal biomarker extraction by preventing low-quality B-scans from entering automated segmentation workflows.
method: Compared scalar NR-IQA metrics (BRISQUE, NIQE, PIQE, SNR, PSNR) against pretrained feature embeddings as quality gates.
Evaluated general-purpose ImageNet models and retinal foundation models using supervised linear probing and unsupervised K-Means clustering.
Used choroid segmentation on 6,076 OCT B-scans from 80 subjects as the prototype task.
evidence_signal: All scalar metrics were weak predictors of segmentation success (|r| < 0.20), while learned representations improved discrimination, reaching ROC-AUC up to 0.77 for ImageNet models and about 0.81 for RETFound.
watch_item: The results are task- and model-specific, so a gate that works for choroid segmentation may not transfer directly to other OCT tasks or devices without revalidation.
paper_title: Task-Specific Quality Gating for Retinal Optical Coherence Tomography B-Scans: Learned Representations Over Scalar Metrics in Choroid Segmentation
